form.name: intro
form.label: Web Calendar: a calendar web app with a CalDAV gateway. It always installs the app. It can also install its own Kanidm (sign-in) and Radicale (calendar store), or use ones you already run. Every setting below has a short description; the defaults are the ones of the project's docker-compose.yml. Values must not contain double quotes or backslashes.

form.name: bundleKanidmInfo
form.label: Kanidm signs users in (OpenID Connect) and holds the groups. Tick the box to install a new Kanidm next to the app; you choose its address further down, with the address of the app. Untick it to use a Kanidm you already run (you enter its issuer URL below).

form.name: bundleKanidm
form.label: Install a Kanidm server for this app

form.name: bundleRadicaleInfo
form.label: Radicale stores the calendars. Tick the box to install a new Radicale on a private network only the app can reach. Untick it to use a Radicale you already run; it must then be configured as described in deploy/cosmos/README.md.

form.name: bundleRadicale
form.label: Install a Radicale server for this app

form.name: appImageInfo
form.label: Image: the container image of the app. Cosmos pulls it from a registry, so it must be pushed there first (deploy/cosmos/README.md shows how). Use a version tag rather than latest so an update is your decision.

form.name: appImage
form.label: App image

form.name: autoUpdateInfo
form.label: Automatic updates: Cosmos pulls a newer image under the same tag and restarts the app on its own. Leave it off if you want to read the release notes and back up first.

form.name: autoUpdate
form.label: Update the app image automatically

form.name: kanidmImageInfo
form.label: Kanidm image: keep a fixed version. Kanidm upgrades one minor version at a time, so never jump versions.

form.name: kanidmImage
form.label: Kanidm image

form.name: kanidmLogLevelInfo
form.label: Kanidm log level: info for normal operation, debug or trace only while looking for a problem (they log much more).

form.name: kanidmLogLevel
form.label: Kanidm log level

form.name: radicaleImageInfo
form.label: Radicale image: the Radicale project's own image. The app is tested with 3.9.0.

form.name: radicaleImage
form.label: Radicale image

form.name: radicaleLogLevelInfo
form.label: Radicale log level: info logs every request; warning or error log less.

form.name: radicaleLogLevel
form.label: Radicale log level

form.name: oidcIssuerBundledInfo
form.label: Issuer: set for you as https://(Kanidm address)/oauth2/openid/(client id below). After the install, create the client in Kanidm as the post-install notes say.

form.name: oidcIssuerInfo
form.label: Issuer (NUXT_OIDC_ISSUER, required): the issuer URL of the app's client in your Kanidm. An https URL that ends with the client id, for example https://idm.example.org/oauth2/openid/web-calendar (docs/kanidm-setup.md section 2).

form.name: oidcIssuer
form.label: Kanidm issuer URL

form.name: oidcClientIdInfo
form.label: Client id (NUXT_OIDC_CLIENT_ID): the name of the app's OAuth2 client in Kanidm. Change it only if the client has another name; the issuer must end with it.

form.name: oidcClientId
form.label: OAuth2 client id

form.name: oidcAllowedClientsInfo
form.label: Further clients (NUXT_OIDC_ALLOWED_CLIENTS): other Kanidm clients whose tokens the CalDAV gateway accepts, comma-separated. Empty means only the client above.

form.name: oidcAllowedClients
form.label: Further accepted clients

form.name: oidcAdminGroupInfo
form.label: Admin group (NUXT_OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP): the Kanidm group whose members are admins of the app. Must not be empty.

form.name: oidcAdminGroup
form.label: Admin group

form.name: oidcKeyMaxAgeInfo
form.label: Signing key cache (NUXT_OIDC_KEY_MAX_AGE_SEC): seconds the app uses Kanidm's signing keys before it fetches them again. A key Kanidm removed is trusted for at most this long. A whole number, at least 1.

form.name: oidcKeyMaxAge
form.label: Signing key cache (seconds)

form.name: tokenHashKeyInfo
form.label: App token key (NUXT_TOKEN_HASH_KEY, required): hashes the app tokens that calendar apps sign in with. At least 32 characters; a random one is filled in. Keep it: changing it signs every calendar app out. Rotate it with the next field instead.

form.name: tokenHashKey
form.label: App token key

form.name: tokenHashKeysInfo
form.label: Key rotation (NUXT_TOKEN_HASH_KEYS): more keys as version:key entries separated by commas, the current key first, for example 2:(new key). The key above stays valid as version 1. Empty means only the key above.

form.name: tokenHashKeys
form.label: Rotated app token keys

form.name: sealKeyInfo
form.label: External account key (NUXT_EXTERNAL_SEAL_KEY): seals the passwords of external CalDAV accounts. 32 random bytes as base64 or 64 hex characters; generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32. Empty turns accounts with a login off. Changing it makes users enter their passwords again.

form.name: sealKey
form.label: External account key

form.name: groupSyncTokenInfo
form.label: Group sync token (NUXT_GROUP_SYNC_TOKEN): the read-only API token of the Kanidm service account that copies group membership to Radicale (docs/kanidm-setup.md section 3). You only get it after setting Kanidm up: leave it empty now and add it later in the app container's environment. Without it, group shares do not work.

form.name: groupSyncToken
form.label: Group sync token

form.name: groupSyncIntervalInfo
form.label: Group sync interval (NUXT_GROUP_SYNC_INTERVAL_SEC): seconds between group-sync runs. A removed group member keeps access for up to this long; at most 300.

form.name: groupSyncInterval
form.label: Group sync interval (seconds)

form.name: radicaleWarning
form.label: Your Radicale must trust the X-Remote-User header (auth type http_x_remote_user), so anything that can reach it can act as any user. Only the app may be able to reach it: no published port, no route in Cosmos, a network shared with the app only. Its other settings are listed in deploy/cosmos/README.md.

form.name: radicaleUrlInfo
form.label: Radicale URL (NUXT_RADICALE_URL): the internal address the app reaches your Radicale at, for example http://radicale:5232.

form.name: radicaleUrl
form.label: Radicale URL

form.name: radicaleNetworkInfo
form.label: Radicale network: the Docker network your Radicale is on, so the app can join it. Empty if the app reaches it another way.

form.name: radicaleNetwork
form.label: Docker network of your Radicale

form.name: gatewayCorsInfo
form.label: CORS origins (NUXT_GATEWAY_CORS_ORIGINS): origins of external browser apps that may call the CalDAV gateway, comma-separated, for example https://other.example.org. Empty means none.

form.name: gatewayCors
form.label: CalDAV CORS origins

form.name: gatewayMaxBodyInfo
form.label: Largest upload (NUXT_GATEWAY_MAX_BODY_BYTES): the largest request body the CalDAV gateway forwards, in bytes. 10485760 is 10 MiB.

form.name: gatewayMaxBody
form.label: Largest CalDAV request (bytes)

form.name: gatewayMaxConcurrentInfo
form.label: Parallel requests (NUXT_GATEWAY_MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_USER): requests one signed-in user may have in flight at once; more get 429 for a second. Raise it only if a calendar app of yours legitimately opens more.

form.name: gatewayMaxConcurrent
form.label: Parallel requests per user

form.name: trustForwardedForInfo
form.label: Trust the proxy (NUXT_GATEWAY_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR): the failed-login throttle takes the client address from X-Forwarded-For, which the Cosmos proxy adds. Keep it on while Cosmos is the only way to reach the app (this template publishes no port). Off, every client shares the proxy's address and one attacker can lock everyone out of the password login.

form.name: trustForwardedFor
form.label: Trust X-Forwarded-For from the Cosmos proxy

form.name: outboundHostsInfo
form.label: Allowed hosts (NUXT_OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS): hosts the server may contact for its users (iCal subscriptions, external CalDAV accounts), comma-separated: exact names (cal.example.org) or domains (*.example.org). With a list, a script that got into the page can only reach these hosts.

form.name: outboundHosts
form.label: Allowed outbound hosts

form.name: outboundAnyInfo
form.label: Any host (NUXT_OUTBOUND_ALLOW_ANY_HOST): with no list above, lets the server contact any public host its users name, for example for public calendar feeds from many sites. Ignored when a list is set.

form.name: outboundAny
form.label: Allow any public host

form.name: outboundError
form.label: Fill in the allowed hosts or tick Allow any public host: the app does not start with neither.

form.name: icalCacheTtlInfo
form.label: Feed cache (NUXT_ICAL_PROXY_CACHE_TTL_SEC): seconds a fetched .ics subscription is served without asking its source again; 0 always asks.

form.name: icalCacheTtl
form.label: Subscription cache (seconds)

form.name: icalMaxBytesInfo
form.label: Largest feed (NUXT_ICAL_PROXY_MAX_BYTES): the largest .ics file the server fetches, in bytes. 5242880 is 5 MiB.

form.name: icalMaxBytes
form.label: Largest subscription (bytes)

form.name: icalTimeoutInfo
form.label: Feed timeout (NUXT_ICAL_PROXY_TIMEOUT_MS): milliseconds allowed for fetching one .ics file.

form.name: icalTimeout
form.label: Subscription timeout (ms)

form.name: sharingReconcileInfo
form.label: Sharing check (NUXT_SHARING_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SEC): seconds between the runs that turn the access rules into Radicale shares; at most 900. Changes made in the app apply at once anyway.

form.name: sharingReconcile
form.label: Sharing check interval (seconds)

form.name: sharingAuditInfo
form.label: Sharing audit (NUXT_SHARING_AUDIT_INTERVAL_HOURS): hours between the consistency audits of every calendar home, 1 to 168.

form.name: sharingAudit
form.label: Sharing audit interval (hours)

form.name: sharingOwnersInfo
form.label: Shared owners (NUXT_SHARING_SHARED_OWNERS): service principals whose calendars appear as shared calendars, comma-separated, each starting with an underscore, for example _team. Empty means none.

form.name: sharingOwners
form.label: Shared calendar owners

form.name: resourcesReconcileInfo
form.label: Booking check (NUXT_RESOURCES_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SEC): seconds between the checks of booked events for moves and deletions; at most 900.

form.name: resourcesReconcile
form.label: Booking check interval (seconds)

form.name: resourcesManagerCancelInfo
form.label: Managers cancel (NUXT_RESOURCES_MANAGER_CANCEL): a manager of a resource (a room, a car) may cancel other people's bookings of it. Off, only the person who booked can cancel.

form.name: resourcesManagerCancel
form.label: Managers may cancel bookings of others

form.name: timeZoneInfo
form.label: Time zone (TZ): the organization's IANA time zone, for example Europe/Berlin. The app shows and plans times in it by default.

form.name: timeZone
form.label: Time zone

form.name: demoInfo
form.label: Demo mode (NUXT_DEMO): the page skips the sign-in and shows made-up data. For previews only; never for real use. The server logs a warning while it is on.

form.name: demo
form.label: Demo mode

form.name: useHostFoldersInfo
form.label: Storage: by default each kind of data gets its own Docker volume. Tick the box to keep it in folders on the host instead (easier to back up with your own tools). Leave a name or path empty for the default shown in its description.

form.name: useHostFolders
form.label: Store data in host folders instead of Docker volumes

form.name: appDataInfo
form.label: App data, mounted at /data: the app's SQLite database (app tokens, access rules, settings, bookings, audit log). Back it up. Default: the volume (service name)-data, or the folder (Cosmos storage)/(service name)/data.

form.name: appDataPath
form.label: Host folder for the app data

form.name: appDataVolume
form.label: Volume for the app data

form.name: groupsInfo
form.label: Group file, mounted at /groups: the file htgroup, which the app writes from Kanidm's groups and Radicale reads. With your own Radicale, pick a volume or folder that Radicale reads too. Default: the volume (service name)-groups, or the folder (Cosmos storage)/(service name)/groups.

form.name: groupsPath
form.label: Host folder for the group file

form.name: groupsVolume
form.label: Volume for the group file

form.name: radicaleDataInfo
form.label: Calendars, mounted at /var/lib/radicale: every calendar and event, and Radicale's share list. Back it up. Default: the volume (service name)-radicale-data, or the folder (Cosmos storage)/(service name)/radicale.

form.name: radicaleDataPath
form.label: Host folder for the calendars

form.name: radicaleDataVolume
form.label: Volume for the calendars

form.name: kanidmDataInfo
form.label: Kanidm data, mounted at /data: the Kanidm database (users, groups, credentials) and its TLS certificate. Back it up. Default: the volume (service name)-kanidm-data, or the folder (Cosmos storage)/(service name)/kanidm.

form.name: kanidmDataPath
form.label: Host folder for the Kanidm data

form.name: kanidmDataVolume
form.label: Volume for the Kanidm data

post-install.name: open
post-install.label: The app is at https://{Hostnames.{StaticServiceName}.{StaticServiceName}.host}/ once sign-in is set up.

post-install.name: kanidmSetup
post-install.label: Set Kanidm up: 1. Get the admin password with: docker exec {ServiceName}-kanidm kanidmd recover-account idm_admin. 2. Follow docs/kanidm-setup.md with the server https://{Hostnames.{StaticServiceName}-kanidm.{StaticServiceName}-kanidm.host}: create the groups, the client {Context.oidcClientId} with the redirect URL https://{Hostnames.{StaticServiceName}.{StaticServiceName}.host}/auth/callback, and the group-sync account. 3. Put its token into NUXT_GROUP_SYNC_TOKEN in the environment of the container {ServiceName} and restart it.

post-install.name: kanidmExisting
post-install.label: In your Kanidm, follow docs/kanidm-setup.md: the client {Context.oidcClientId} needs the redirect URL https://{Hostnames.{StaticServiceName}.{StaticServiceName}.host}/auth/callback. Put the group-sync token into NUXT_GROUP_SYNC_TOKEN in the environment of the container {ServiceName} if you have not yet.

post-install.name: radicaleExisting
post-install.label: Check that your Radicale is reachable by the app only and reads the group file the app writes (deploy/cosmos/README.md).

routes.name: {ServiceName}
routes.description: The calendar web app and its CalDAV gateway (/caldav/)

{ServiceName}-radicale.command: --server-hosts 0.0.0.0:5232 --server-max-content-length 10485760 --auth-type http_x_remote_user --rights-type owner_only --group-type htgroup --group-htgroup-filename /etc/radicale/groups/htgroup --sharing-type csv --sharing-database-path /var/lib/radicale/sharing.csv --sharing-collection-by-map True --sharing-permit-create-map True --storage-filesystem-folder /var/lib/radicale/collections --storage-predefined-collections {"def-calendar":{"C:supported-calendar-component-set":"VEVENT,VJOURNAL,VTODO","D:displayname":"Personal\u0020Calendar","tag":"VCALENDAR"}} --web-type none --logging-level {Context.radicaleLogLevel}

routes.name: {ServiceName}-kanidm
routes.description: Kanidm, the sign-in server of the calendar
